```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(RcmdrShiny)
```

# Overview

The Chart Studio is the **Charts** tab in Studio mode. It is a builder, a live
preview and a gallery built on top of the plotting engine used by the Rcmdr
dialogs. Applying a chart always produces the same reproducible command the
equivalent dialog would produce.

The lifecycle is **spec -> preview -> apply -> gallery -> reopen**.

# A specification is a list

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::chart_spec(
  "histogram", "Dataset",
  mapping = list(x = "score"),
  labels = list(title = "Score distribution")
)
```

The spec records the data set, the mapping, the type-specific options, the
theme, the labels and the output size. `RcmdrShiny:::chart_types()` lists the available
types.

```{r}
names(RcmdrShiny:::chart_types())
```

# The generated command

With the default theme and no labels, `RcmdrShiny:::chart_spec_command()` is exactly the
command of the matching dialog.

```{r}
spec <- RcmdrShiny:::chart_spec("histogram", "Dataset", list(x = "score"))
RcmdrShiny:::chart_spec_command(spec)
```

Theme and labels are additive: they only appear when the user changes them.

```{r}
spec$theme$palette <- "colorblind"
spec$labels$title <- "Score distribution"
RcmdrShiny:::chart_spec_command(spec)
```

# Preview

`RcmdrShiny:::chart_preview()` renders a PNG in an isolated environment. It does not run a
command, does not touch the log and does not add a plot to the gallery.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
state <- AppState()
result <- RcmdrShiny:::chart_preview(state, spec)
result$type
result$error
```

# Apply

`RcmdrShiny:::chart_apply()` runs the command through `run_command()` and attaches the spec
to the resulting plot.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
result <- RcmdrShiny:::chart_apply(state, spec)
result$ok
result$index
```

# Gallery

`RcmdrShiny:::plot_list()` returns one row per plot, with title, type, data set, time and
pinned state. Search, filter and pin without touching the command log.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::plot_list(state, query = "distribution", pinned = FALSE)
RcmdrShiny:::plot_update(state, 1, title = "Pinned distribution", pinned = TRUE)
```

The gallery actions map to small pure functions:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::plot_reopen(state, 1)      # the spec attached to the plot
RcmdrShiny:::plot_compare(state, c(1, 2))
RcmdrShiny:::plot_delete(state, 1)
```

# Round-trip

A reopened spec can be changed and applied again.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
reopened <- RcmdrShiny:::plot_reopen(state, 1)
reopened$options$scale <- "density"
RcmdrShiny:::chart_apply(state, reopened)
```

# Export

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::plot_export(state, 1, "png", "chart.png", width = 1200, height = 800)
RcmdrShiny:::plot_export(state, 1, "pdf", "chart.pdf")
RcmdrShiny:::plot_export(state, 1, "svg", "chart.svg")
```

SVG export uses `svglite` when available and falls back to the cairo device.
HTML export is available for interactive plots built with `plotly`.

# Interactive selection

Supported charts also have a plotly expression. For an ungrouped scatterplot,
select points and create a subset:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rows <- c(1, 3, 5)
command <- sprintf("Selected <- Dataset[c(%s), , drop = FALSE]",
                   paste(rows, collapse = ", "))
run_command(state, command)
```

The subset is a normal command and the new data set becomes active.

# ggplot2 engine

Installing `ggplot2` enables a full alternative engine for all 11 chart types.
The builder adds facet, size and label mappings only in this mode, plus alpha,
position, bin width, smooth method and band, jitter, shape, coordinate flip,
facet scales/columns and a ggplot2 theme. Labels support title, subtitle, tag,
axis labels and caption; palettes and log axes become ggplot2 scales.

The applied command is a single `print(ggplot(...))`; the base `palette()`,
`par()` and `title()` calls are never mixed in. Previews, apply, gallery and
export reuse the same command path.

If the installed `plotly` and `ggplot2` versions can convert ggplot objects,
the gallery also offers the interactive version and HTML export.

# Boxplot, histogram and scatter options

The boxplot builder exposes notch, notch width, variable width, horizontal
layout, outlier visibility and box width. Horizontal uses `boxplot()` in the
base engine (car refuses it) and `coord_flip()` in ggplot2; the common jitter
control overlays points in ggplot2.

The histogram scale selector is honoured by both engines. The scatterplot adds
a regression line, a confidence ellipse, a grid and jitter; ggplot2 maps the
smooth choice and the confidence band to `geom_smooth(method=, se=)` and the
ellipse to `stat_ellipse()`.

The preview is isolated: it never logs a command or adds a plot. When an
interactive expression exists, the Build panel shows the plotly widget (hover,
zoom, selection); the builder uses its own source and an ungrouped scatterplot
can create a data set from the selection with the same command as the gallery.
Otherwise the static PNG is shown.

# ggplot-only types

Four statistical types are available only with the ggplot2 engine: violin plot
(trim, scale, bandwidth, optional boxplot), empirical CDF (padding, line
style), 2D density (bins, bandwidth, points) and heatmap (two variables plus a
numeric value, low/high gradient and optional labels). The type selector is
filtered by engine; the base engine rejects these types explicitly.

# Remaining chart options

Density exposes kernel, adjust, rug and grid (adjust in ggplot2). Line graphs
support line/step/area, style and width, with optional colour grouping in
ggplot2. Bar graphs expose width and count/percent statistics. Dot plots add
binning and ggplot2 bin axis/stack direction/size. Strip charts control jitter
and point shape. QQ plots choose the distribution, reference line, envelope and
grid. Plots of means connect the means and control error-bar width and point
size. XY plots combine points/lines with an optional smooth and layout.

# Design notes

- The base engine remains the default; ggplot2 is opt-in.
- The applied command is the dialog command, plus palette and labels only when
  the user changes them.
- Previews and gallery metadata are session state, not commands.
- Every plot keeps its specification, so the round-trip is exact for the
  supported types.
